t.1.10.1: And further still, O lord of kings, hear from me these beneficial words, just as that wise foremost of the gods related them.
t.1.10.2: Born in the lineage of the Ikṣvākus, there will be a most righteous king, Daśaratha by name, glorious and true to his promises.
t.1.10.3: That king will have a friendship with the king of the Aṅgas, and he will have a most fortunate daughter named Śāntā.
t.1.10.4: The son of King Aṅga is known by the name Romapāda. To him the illustrious King Daśaratha will go.
t.1.10.7: And having received that brahmin, the king, freed from his anxiety, will perform that sacrifice with a joyful inner heart.
t.1.10.5: I am childless, O righteous-souled one. Let him whose wife is Śāntā, commanded by you, perform my sacrifice for the sake of continuing my family line.
t.1.10.6: Then, having heard those words of the king and pondered them in his mind, that self-possessed one will send forth Śāntā's husband, through whom sons are to be won.
t.1.10.8: And King Daśaratha, knower of dharma, desiring to perform a sacrifice, will with folded hands choose him, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, the foremost of the twice-born.
t.1.10.9: For the sake of sacrifice, for the sake of offspring, and for the sake of heaven, the lord of men, the protector of the people, obtains that desire of his from the foremost of the twice-born.
t.1.10.10: And to him there will be born four sons of boundless valour, who will establish and uphold his lineage and will be renowned throughout all the worlds.
t.1.10.11: Thus, long ago in the age of the gods, the blessed and mighty Sanatkumāra, foremost among the gods, related this tale in former times.
t.1.10.12: Therefore, O tiger among men, O great king, go yourself with your army and your mounts, and bring him here, treating him with the highest honor.
t.1.10.13: Having obtained Vasiṣṭha's consent and having heard the charioteer's words, he set out with the women of his inner apartments and with his ministers to the place where that twice-born one was.
t.1.10.14: Slowly crossing forests and rivers, he approached the region where the foremost of sages dwelt.
t.1.10.15: Having approached, he first beheld that best of the twice-born, the sage's son, seated near Romapāda and blazing like a fire.
t.1.10.16: Then the king, with a heart full of joy, paid him homage according to custom, and with special distinction, because of his friendship with that king.
t.1.10.17: Romapāda told the wise son of the sage of his friendship and kinship with the king, and then the sage's son honored him in return.
t.1.10.18: Thus well honored by him, the king, a bull among men, having stayed with him for seven or eight days, spoke these words to the king.
t.1.10.19: O king, lord of the people, let your daughter Śāntā go with her husband to my city, for a great undertaking is at hand.
t.1.10.20: Saying “So be it,” the king consented to the departure of that wise one and spoke these words to the brahmin: “Go, together with your wife.”
t.1.10.21: Then the sage's son, giving his promise, said to the king, "So be it." Permitted by the king, he set out together with his wife.
t.1.10.22: The two of them, Daśaratha and the valiant Romapāda, having saluted each other with joined palms and embraced breast to breast out of affection, rejoiced.
t.1.10.23: Then, having taken leave of his friend, the delight of the Raghus set out and sent swift-moving messengers to the citizens, saying: "Let the whole city be quickly and splendidly adorned."
t.1.10.24: Then those citizens, delighted on hearing that the king had arrived, carried out everything just as the king had commanded at that time.
t.1.10.25: Then the king, placing that bull among the twice-born at the head, entered the well-adorned city amid the resounding blasts of conches and kettledrums.
t.1.10.26: Then all the townspeople were filled with delight when they saw the twice-born sage being honoured and led into the city by the lord of men, whose deeds were like Indra's.
t.1.10.27: Having led him into the inner apartments and honored him with worship according to the scriptures, he then considered himself to have fulfilled his purpose, since he had brought him there.
t.1.10.28: Seeing large-eyed Śāntā arrived in this way together with her husband, all the inner apartments of the palace were filled with joyful delight.
t.1.10.29: Honored by those women, and especially by the king, she, the twice-born lady, dwelt there happily for some time together with him.
